text:
alex: heads up — we saw a sustained p99 latency jump (~450ms -> ~1.1s) starting at 14:07 PT right after canary rollout of model v8.0. rolling windows show throughput dip ~18%.
maria: timeline? which hosts/regions?
alex: US-west1 only so far, noisy across two hosts in pool A. spike aligns with 14:05 deploy.
sam: rolling canary ID? any tokenizer changes in v8.0?
alex: canary id c-2026-03-18-8 — yes tokenizer switched to subtoken-v2 and we changed prefetcher/kvcache prewarm to dynamic.
ryan: pinging perf-oncall, starting flamegraph capture on affected hosts.
perf-oncall: got it. grabbing /var/log/runtime/prof-*.svg and rpc traces. will paste snapshot.
perf-oncall: (uploaded) /artifacts/profiles/2407504321/us-west1-hostA-flame.svg
perf-oncall: quick observation: kernel_decider mispredicted kernel path ~84% of calls for short seqlen requests after tokenizer change — leads to extra memcpy + suboptimal kernel chosen. also kvcache miss rate jumped from 2% to 27% for warm prefixes.
maria: that sounds like subtokenization changed token boundaries -> different prefix hashes -> kv fragmentation. did we also change kv eviction thresholds?
alex: prefetch config moved from static 64 to adaptive that keys on token-density. apparently subtoken-v2 increases token count by ~1.6x for chat prompts which trips the adaptive threshold and evicts earlier.
sam: can we reproduce locally? i can run a small harness with v7.9 vs v8.0 token counts and measure kernel selection.
ryan: perf traces show batching heuristics also got confused — the batcher hinter sees more short tokens but overall token arrival rate didn't drop so batcher created smaller micro-batches, increasing per-request overhead.
perf-oncall: stack snippet from kernel_decider: `if (seq_mode == AUTO && seq_est < threshold) choose_fast_kernel(); else choose_general_kernel();` seq_est computed from first N subtokens — with subtoken-v2 early tokens are dense -> underestimation of true seq -> picks fast kernel that later suffers cache misses.
maria: so cascade: tokenizer change -> higher subtoken density -> prefetcher evicts earlier + seq estimator misfires -> kernel misselect -> memcpy + kv misses -> latency spike.
alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back to v7.9 canary 2) force kernel_decider to use general kernel for 5m on affected hosts 3) increase prefetcher threshold temporarily 4) pin prefetch warm keys from recent cache snapshot.
sam: I can push a quick feature-flag to force general kernel on those hosts. takes ~8min to rollout.
ryan: infra-bot: started host-quarantine for us-west1-hostA, hostB (automation) :shield:
infra-bot: action=quarantine hosts=[us-west1-hostA,us-west1-hostB] initiator=ryan ts=2407504820
maria: also want to capture tokenization diffs — @sam can you dump token counts per input for v7.9 and v8.0? put to /tmp/token-diff-240750.log.
sam: on it.
perf-oncall: ran a quick experiment with patched kernel_decider that uses 1.5x seq_est for first 60s — p99 fell back to 480ms in canary.
alex: good signal. I want rollback queued as plan B if flag + threshold bump doesn't hold.
maria: ops — can we bump prefetcher threshold from 64->96 temporarily? that seems lowest-risk.
ryan: will open a deploy for that to affected hosts. ETA 10m.
alex: schedule follow-up postmortem after stabilization. please capture sample traces, the tokenizer diff, kv hit/miss timelines, and batch size histograms for before/after. low-cost fix might be to adjust seq estimator or sample more tokens for estimator.
sam: token diffs: v7.9 avg tokens=82, v8.0 avg subtokens=130 for same prompts. attached gist /tmp/token-diff-240750.log.
perf-oncall: also saw increased memcpy bytes/sec on host NICs — looks like kernel path doing fallback memcpy when kv miss. included mem profile link /artifacts/mem/240750_memprof.txt
alex: OK let's do this order: 1) apply kernel_decider flag on canary hosts (sam) 2) bump prefetch threshold to 96 (ryan) 3) monitor 15m window, if p99 > 700ms rollback canary to v7.9 (alex)
maria: I'll create the incident ticket and add owners + required artifacts checklist.
ryan: rolling prefetch patch now.
perf-oncall: monitoring dashboards — pushing a small alert to #incidents if p99 > 700ms or kv_miss_rate > 10% for 5m.
alex: thanks. noted we need a longer-term fix: update seq_estimator to weight subtoken density (or sample more tokens), and add canary tests that simulate tokenizer changes.
maria: agreed. add model tokenizer diff to model onboarding checklist.
sam: kernel flag landed to canary; observed immediate p99 drop to ~520ms. continuing to watch.
perf-oncall: 15m check currently p99=540ms, kv_miss_rate=6%, throughput back to -3% of baseline.
alex: great. leave the quarantine until fully stable. we'll schedule a deeper perf profiling session tomorrow. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
